notes: SEARCH COVERAGE IS POOR. All web searches were refused (shared session search budget used up), so none of the six required searches ran: not the general AI search, nor the ones on superintelligence, extinction or existential risk, pause/slowdown/moratorium, China agreement or treaty, name plus "AI safety", or a campaign-site-restricted search. Instead I opened pages directly. Opened and read: campaign home, platform, about and four issue pages (no mention of AI except the one bullet quoted), the WIS-TV 28 Oct 2026 interview page, and the American Prospect 8 Oct 2026 profile. Could not open: Politico Magazine 4 Nov 2026 interview, The Hill article, Ballotpedia (empty page, so no candidate questionnaire was checked), and the site searches of the Post and Courier, SC Daily Gazette and SCETV. No debate transcript or candidate questionnaire was found or checked. The campaign site showed no press releases or news items. Three campaign issue pages (healthcare, gun violence, reproductive freedom) were not opened for AI mentions; the healthcare page may contain the Medicare AI item below. Quote caveats: pages were read through a fetch tool that passes the page through a small summarising model, so both quotes should be re-checked character for character by the reviewer; the WIS-TV quote may come from a video transcript or article text and may be a fragment of a longer sentence. The date for the campaign-site statement is the page's publication date (23 Dec 2025); the page was modified 12 Jul 2026 and I cannot tell when the AI bullet was added. Paraphrase left out of statements: the American Prospect (8 Oct 2026, https://prospect.org/2026/10/08/south-carolina-senate-hopeful-runs-on-health-care-populism-annie-andrews/) describes her platform as including "a ban on the use of AI to make decisions on treatment in Medicare"; these are the author's words, not hers, and would be level D in any case. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act and the 23 September 2026 China letter: she was a candidate, not a senator, in September 2026, so she could not have co-sponsored or signed; no source found shows any statement by her on either. Identity: sources are her own campaign site and interviews naming her as the South Carolina Senate candidate, so confusion with another person is unlikely.
